title: This is their 'physical predetermination': physical as opposed to moral causality
source_text: XVII. Et haec est quae ab ipsis dicitur Praedeterminatio, quam etiam Physicam appellant, non prout Physicum, id est, naturale opponitur Supernaturali, sed prout Physicum opponitur Morali. Nimirum volunt Deum Voluntates creatas ad agendum praedeterminare, non simpliciter objectum proponendo, suadendo, alliciendo, quae sunt Causae Moralis propria; sed immediate ipsam Voluntatem movendo, & actionem veram, realem & proprie dictam in eam exercendo, quod est proprium causae quae Physica vocatur.
pass_a_gloss: And this is what is called by them Predetermination, which they also call Physical, not as Physical, that is, natural is opposed to Supernatural, but as Physical is opposed to Moral. Namely they will have it that God predetermines created Wills to acting, not simply by proposing the object, persuading, enticing, which are proper to a Moral Cause; but by immediately moving the Will itself, and exercising on it a true, real and properly so called action, which is proper to a cause which is called Physical.
pass_b_english: This is what they call predetermination, and they also call it physical, not in the sense in which the physical, meaning the natural, is opposed to the supernatural, but in the sense in which the physical is opposed to the moral.

They hold that God predetermines created wills to act not merely by presenting an object, urging and attracting, which is what a moral cause does, but by moving the will itself directly and exerting on it a true, real action in the proper sense, which is what belongs to a cause called physical.

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
